node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Origin on coordinate plane
node.description: Identify the origin as the point where the coordinate axes intersect and as the reference point for coordinates.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: X coordinate horizontal position
node.description: Interpret the x-coordinate as horizontal position measured from the origin.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Y coordinate vertical position
node.description: Interpret the y-coordinate as vertical position measured from the origin.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate signs by quadrant
node.description: Use the signs of x- and y-coordinates to identify or check the quadrant of a point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Read axis scale
node.description: Read coordinate values from axes with labelled increments and consistent scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unequal axis scales
node.description: Interpret graphs where horizontal and vertical axes use different scale intervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant first difference in tables
node.description: Identify linear relationships in tables by checking for a constant first difference when inputs increase evenly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Missing values in linear tables
node.description: Use a linear rule or constant rate of change to fill missing values in a table.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rule from two table rows
node.description: Use two rows of a linear table to determine the rate of change and starting value for a rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare table graph equation
node.description: Connect the same linear relationship across a table, graph and equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Independent dependent variables in contexts
node.description: Identify independent and dependent variables in contextual linear relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context units for gradient
node.description: Interpret gradient units in context, such as dollars per item or metres per second.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context initial value
node.description: Interpret the y-intercept or constant term as the initial value in a contextual linear model.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context domain restrictions
node.description: Restrict inputs of a linear model to values that make sense in the context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Interpolate linear model
node.description: Estimate or calculate values between known data points using a linear model.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Extrapolate linear model
node.description: Use a linear model to predict values beyond the observed or given data range and consider reliability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel lines same gradient
node.description: Recognise that nonvertical parallel lines have the same gradient and different intercepts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line intersection as equal outputs
node.description: Interpret the intersection of two line graphs as an input where both relationships have the same output.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Horizontal line constant output
node.description: Interpret horizontal line graphs as relationships with constant output and zero gradient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertical line constant input
node.description: Interpret vertical line graphs as all points with the same input value and undefined gradient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate order is x then y
node.description: In an ordered pair, the first coordinate gives horizontal position and the second coordinate gives vertical position.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant first difference indicates linear
node.description: When input steps are equal, a constant first difference in outputs indicates a linear relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient units are output per input
node.description: The units of gradient describe how much the output changes for one unit of input.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context domain must make sense
node.description: A contextual linear model should only use input values that are meaningful in the situation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel lines have same gradient
node.description: Nonvertical parallel lines have equal gradients and do not intersect.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ordered pair reversed
node.description: Learner plots or reads an ordered pair as y then x instead of x then y.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant difference with unequal inputs
node.description: Learner treats equal output differences as evidence of a linear rule without checking whether input steps are equal.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient units ignored
node.description: Learner gives a numerical gradient in context without interpreting the units of rate of change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Extrapolation always reliable
node.description: Learner assumes a linear trend remains reliable far beyond the observed data or meaningful context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel lines same intercept
node.description: Learner assumes parallel lines must have the same intercept rather than the same gradient.

edge.rationale: Locating the origin is central to using the coordinate plane.
Interpreting ordered pairs includes identifying the horizontal coordinate.
Coordinate signs are a common way to check quadrant location.
Constant first differences are a core table-based linear-rate check.
Comparing tables, graphs and equations directly practises linear-function representation fluency.
Contextual linear modelling includes interpreting the rate's units.
Parallel-line reasoning uses gradient and intercept information.
Identifying the origin requires recognising the coordinate axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot locate where the horizontal and vertical axes meet.

edge.rationale: Horizontal coordinate position is measured from the origin.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads horizontal position without reference to the origin.

edge.rationale: Coordinate reading usually establishes the horizontal coordinate before the vertical coordinate.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses or confuses coordinate order.

edge.rationale: Interpreting coordinate signs by quadrant requires knowing the four-quadrant plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places points with negative coordinates in the wrong quadrant.

edge.rationale: Reading graph scale requires identifying and using the coordinate axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes each grid interval is one regardless of labels.

edge.rationale: Unequal axis scales are an extension of reading labelled graph scales.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies one axis scale to both axes.

edge.rationale: Checking first differences requires reading input-output table values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares outputs without attending to input spacing.

edge.rationale: Filling missing table values often uses constant rate or first-difference structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner fills values by pattern guessing without maintaining a constant rate.

edge.rationale: Deriving a rule from two rows requires identifying rate of change from the table.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds a rate but cannot recover the initial value or rule.

edge.rationale: Comparing table, graph and equation representations requires graphing linear rules.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot match equivalent relationships across representations.

edge.rationale: Identifying dependent and independent variables builds on interpreting paired quantities in context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps input and output quantities in context.

edge.rationale: Interpreting gradient units depends on understanding gradient as a rate of change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives the gradient as a number without units or contextual meaning.

edge.rationale: Contextual initial value interpretation builds on y-intercept meaning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the starting quantity when input is zero.

edge.rationale: Domain restrictions are applied after a linear equation has been connected to context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts negative time, fractional people or out-of-range inputs without checking context.

edge.rationale: Interpolation uses a contextual linear model to estimate values between known inputs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner estimates values without using the model's rate or equation.

edge.rationale: Extrapolation extends linear-model use beyond interpolation and requires more caution.
edge.failure_signal: Learner extends a trend beyond context without considering reliability.

edge.rationale: Parallel-line reasoning depends on comparing gradients.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares intercepts instead of gradients to decide whether lines are parallel.

edge.rationale: Intersections of line graphs require representing linear rules on the same coordinate plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads only one coordinate or does not interpret equality of outputs.

edge.rationale: Horizontal-line interpretation builds on zero rate of change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a horizontal line as having undefined gradient.

edge.rationale: Vertical-line interpretation builds on recognising undefined gradient for vertical lines.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a vertical line as a function with constant output.
